sections.content:
Clicking the orange diamond outline at (51, 40):
- Purple square moved from (33, 38) to (47, 46) - DOWN 14, RIGHT 8
- New white diamond: W(12) at (49, 40) with purple center p(1) at (51, 40)
- Magenta moved to M(1) at (49, 47)
- The previous white diamond at (20, 25) is gone
- Light blue regions: S(164) reappeared at (22, 25), S(44) and S(109) merged back
So clicking the orange diamond outline ALSO moved the purple square! The purple square is now at (47, 46), much closer to the target diamond at (46, 54).
Distance from (47, 46) to (46, 54) = 1 + 8 = 9. Getting closer!
Now I see the pattern more clearly:
- Clicking ANYWHERE on the board (light blue regions, orange diamond outline) moves the purple square
- The purple square moves toward the click location
- A white diamond appears at/near the click location
- The purple square is guided by the white diamond
So the mechanic is: click somewhere to move the purple square toward that location. The orange square doesn't seem to move at all.
Wait, but the orange square was at (12, 27) from the start and never moved. Maybe the orange square is already in its final position? Or maybe I need to do something different to move it?
Let me think about what completes the level. The purple square needs to reach (46, 54). It's currently at (47, 46). I need to click somewhere near (46, 54) to guide it there.
But wait - the purple square is now at (47, 46) and the target diamond G(12) is at (46, 54). The white diamond W(12) is at (49, 40). The purple square might automatically move toward the white diamond...
Actually, let me look at the pattern again. Each time I click, the purple square moves. It seems to move toward the click location. So if I click near (46, 54), the purple square should move closer to it.
Let me try clicking near the target diamond at (46, 54).

        print(f"  {c}: px={px}, pos=({b[0]},{b[1]})")
